blinding_guess.why: rclcpp at this revision never calls the five rmw publisher/event functions directly; it reaches them only through rcl wrappers, so any mismatch on these elements would sit in rcl or an rmw implementation, which the snapshot does not show. The tests skip event-callback tests on rmw_connextdds, but that says nothing about a defect in rclcpp itself.

notes: All five packet elements are consumed rmw C API functions. A full-text search of the whole snapshot (rclcpp, rclcpp_action, rclcpp_components, rclcpp_lifecycle; sources, headers, tests, CMake, package.xml) finds no call to rmw_create_publisher, rmw_destroy_publisher, rmw_event_fini, rmw_event_set_callback or rmw_publisher_event_init. rmw_event_set_callback appears only as a doxygen \sa (event_handler.hpp:158) and in test comments (test/rclcpp/test_qos_event.cpp:317, 363, 442, 486: 'rmw_connextdds doesn't support rmw_event_set_callback() interface', used to GTEST_SKIP on rmw_connextdds); the other four names do not appear at all. rclcpp instead calls the rcl-layer functions: rcl_publisher_init (src/rclcpp/publisher_base.cpp:73), rcl_publisher_fini (publisher_base.cpp:59), rcl_publisher_event_init (passed as init_func in include/rclcpp/publisher_base.hpp:333), rcl_event_fini (src/rclcpp/event_handler.cpp:42) and rcl_event_set_callback (event_handler.cpp:79). That these rcl functions forward to the named rmw functions is inferred from naming only; rcl sources are outside the allowed sources and were not read. Because rclcpp does not call the elements itself, no ports were recorded; declares and not_declared are empty because every element is on the consumes side. rclcpp does call other rmw functions directly (e.g. rmw_get_gid_for_publisher at publisher_base.cpp:99, rmw_serialize, rmw_qos_profile_check_compatible), none of which are packet elements. Publisher event types bound in PublisherBase::bind_event_callbacks: RCL_PUBLISHER_OFFERED_DEADLINE_MISSED, RCL_PUBLISHER_LIVELINESS_LOST, RCL_PUBLISHER_OFFERED_INCOMPATIBLE_QOS, RCL_PUBLISHER_INCOMPATIBLE_TYPE, RCL_PUBLISHER_MATCHED (publisher_base.cpp:135-190); only the incompatible-QoS and incompatible-type registrations tolerate RCL_RET_UNSUPPORTED. The package.xml declares <depend>rcl</depend> and <depend>rmw</depend> (lines 37, 41). No dependency definition files were needed (no message elements).
